labels.text: The European Central Bank and Bank of England raise their interest rates by 0.5 percentage points to combat inflation, one day after the US Federal Reserve raises its federal funds rate by 0.25 percentage points.
The United Kingdom and the European Union reach an agreement surrounding modifications to the Northern Ireland Protocol.
The coronation of Charles III and Camilla as King and Queen of the United Kingdom and the other Commonwealth realms is held in Westminster Abbey, London.
The Eurovision Song Contest 2023 is held in Liverpool, UK. Swedish contestant Loreen wins with the song "Tattoo".
The 2023 FIFA Women's World Cup is held in Australia and New Zealand. In the final, Spain wins 1–0 against England.
After British regulators' approval, Microsoft closes its US$68.7 billion acquisition of Activision Blizzard.
The first AI Safety Summit takes place in the United Kingdom, with 28 countries signing a "world first agreement" on how to manage the riskiest forms of artificial intelligence.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange leaves the United Kingdom after being freed from prison in a plea deal with the United States. He returns to his native Australia two days later.
2024 United Kingdom general election: Sir Keir Starmer leads the Labour Party to victory, returning the party to government for the first time in 14 years.
2024 United Kingdom riots: Far-right riots break out throughout the United Kingdom in response to a mass stabbing in Southport, England.
The UK becomes the first G7 country to phase out coal power for electric generation, after 142 years of using the energy source.
Justin Welby announces his resignation as Archbishop of Canterbury following the publication of a report critical of his handling of the abuse of children within the Church of England by John Smyth.
Storm Éowyn hits Ireland and the United Kingdom. Record high wind speeds of 183 kph are recorded in Ireland, while over a million homes are left without power.
A major power outage causes Heathrow Airport in London to completely shut down, with disruption expected to last for days, affecting thousands of flights around the world.
The 2025 Women's Rugby World Cup is held in, and is won by, England.
The UK, Canada, and Australia announce their formal recognition of Palestine as a sovereign state, with France also doing so the next day.
Sarah Mullally becomes the first female primate of the Church of England and Archbishop of Canterbury.
The 2026 Women's T20 World Cup is held in England and Wales, and is won by Australia.
Keir Starmer announces his resignation as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, prompting a leadership election.
The world record for the mile run is broken by British runner Josh Kerr at the London Athletics Meet, with a time of 3:42.66 surpassing the previous record held by Hicham El Guerrouj since 1999.
Andy Burnham is appointed by King Charles III as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, succeeding Keir Starmer.
The 2026 Commonwealth Games are held in Glasgow, Scotland.
Twelve countries, including Canada, France and the United Kingdom, announce plans to introduce or support trade restrictions on goods from Israeli settlements, citing threats to a two-state solution.
